entries.core_move: Interpret $e^{st}$ as the generalized continuous-time exponential form that unifies real exponentials, complex exponentials, and the damped or growing sinusoidal signals developed next.
Decompose $s=\sigma+j\omega$ in $e^{st}=e^{\sigma t}e^{j\omega t}$ to identify $\sigma$ as the growth-or-decay envelope rate and $\omega$ as the oscillation rate of a generalized exponential signal.
Interpret pure real exponentials by setting $s=\sigma$ in $e^{st}$ and using the sign and magnitude of $\sigma$ to determine non-oscillatory growth, decay, or constancy over time.

Convert $e^{st}$ with $s=j\omega$ into $e^{j\omega t}=\cos(\omega t)+j\sin(\omega t)$ to interpret pure complex exponentials as constant-magnitude rotating phasors rather than growing or decaying signals.

Interpret $e^{(\sigma+j\omega)t}$ with $\sigma<0$ as a damped sinusoid by separating the decaying envelope $e^{\sigma t}$ from the oscillatory factor $e^{j\omega t}$ and identifying the resulting amplitude decay rate and angular frequency.
Classify growing sinusoids within $e^{st}$ by recognizing $\sigma>0$ in $s=\sigma+j\omega$, interpreting $e^{\sigma t}$ as the increasing envelope and $\omega$ as the oscillation rate.

Identify the exponential envelope $e^{\sigma t}$ that bounds the oscillatory components of $e^{(\sigma+j\omega)t}$ and use the sign of $\sigma$ to interpret damping, growth, or constant-amplitude behavior.

Determine whether and with what fundamental period the pure complex exponential $e^{j\omega t}$ repeats by enforcing $e^{j\omega(t+T)}=e^{j\omega t}$ and deriving $T_0=2\pi/|\omega|$ for $\omega\neq0$ within the generalized exponential signal family.
